claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse near-surface grain structure.
Post-deposition rapid thermal annealing will significantly refine the coating's near-surface grains.
Rapid thermal annealing activates near-surface dynamic recrystallization that reduces grain size.
A refined near-surface grain structure facilitates formation of a hard, ultra-nanocrystalline tribolayer during sliding.
The sliding-induced tribolayer is cohesive and self-strengthening.
A developed tribolayer suppresses localized shear banding in the coating.
High-entropy alloys can undergo abrupt slip events that appear as stress drops or serrations in certain temperature and strain-rate regimes.
The annealed coating will undergo more homogeneous microscopic deformation, with fewer or smaller stress drops, than the untreated coating.
The annealed coating will have lower wear volume than the untreated coating during high-temperature sliding.
The annealed coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the untreated coating during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted improvements should hold at elevated temperatures where dynamic recrystallization and tribolayer formation are feasible.
At extremely high temperatures or under excessive thermal softening, the predicted improvements may not hold.
Hard tribofilms can contribute to good wear resistance in an HEA coating.
Prior evidence supports a beneficial role of refined microstructures in the wear resistance of similar HEA coatings.
The optimal annealing temperature, annealing duration, and grain-size threshold for FeNiCrCoCu coatings remain undetermined.
